=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- CLAUDE.md:885-895 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The -resend fallback only checks `git ls-remote --heads origin` for a name collision, not local branches, so a leftover local `<branch>-resend` makes `git checkout -b` fail. The same procedure is in .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-236 and workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-236.
  WHY: The documented `-resend-2` fallback never triggers when only a local branch exists, so the session fails at branch creation. Reviewers rated this NIT, and the line ranges they cited differ slightly (885-890 and 891-895).
- .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The doc says the guard unconditionally allows the resend push. When GitHub is unreachable, the git history fallback returns inconclusive and the guard asks for confirmation. The same text is in workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242.
  WHY: The claim holds only when the GitHub API answers, so a session during an outage gets a prompt instead of the documented no-ask push. Reviewers rated this NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Implement the new §21.F logic as standing permission to push to a `<branch>-resend` branch when a force-push is refused ("it is now the default and the session takes it without asking").
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (or the automation logic controlling the agent's push behavior)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The PR diff changes only CLAUDE.md, .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md, workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md and a changelog fragment, with no changes to Python hooks, orchestration or session-management logic. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected this gap as invalid. Its reasons were that the PR description says "No guard, settings or workflow changes" and that CLAUDE.md §21.F is itself the enforcement vehicle.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- CLAUDE.md:885-890 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The instruction for creating the fallback branch is vulnerable to local branch name collisions.
  WHY: The instructions check only `git ls-remote --heads origin`, so a leftover local `<branch>-resend` makes `git checkout -b` fail with "already exists". The same fix is needed in .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md and workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md.
- .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The documentation incorrectly asserts that the guard unconditionally allows the resend push.
  WHY: If the GitHub API is unreachable, the git history fallback classifies the new branch as inconclusive and the guard requests confirmation. The same fix is needed in workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md.
- TASK_GAP | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Requirement: Implement the new §21.F logic as standing permission to push to a `<branch>-resend` branch when a force-push is refused, as described in the PR description and summarized in the changelog.
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (or the automation logic controlling the agent's push behavior).
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff only implements the documentation changes in CLAUDE.md, .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md, workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md, and adds a changelog fragment. The PR description states "New §21.F makes that the default, with no question" and "it is now the default and the session takes it without asking". No changes in Python hooks, orchestration, or session-management logic implement this behavior, so the documentation claims are unsupported by the code.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- CLAUDE.md:892-895 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback checks whether the candidate branch exists on origin, but not locally, so a local-only branch left by a previous fallback can make `git checkout -b <branch>-resend` fail.
  WHY: After an earlier resend push is refused, the local branch exists while origin has none, so retrying fails at branch creation instead of using the documented suffix fallback. The same procedure appears in .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-236 and workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-236.
- .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: "The guard allows this push" is unconditional, but the guard asks for confirmation when GitHub is unreachable and git history is inconclusive.
  WHY: For a resend branch based on the default branch, the history fallback is inconclusive, and the guard requests confirmation for a remote push, contrary to the no-ask instructions. This is specified in CLAUDE.md:860-862 and implemented in .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:2283-2300. The claim is mirrored in workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- CLAUDE.md:891-895 (mirrored at .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-236 and workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-236) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The "name taken" check in the -resend fallback loop is only `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>-resend`, so a leftover local `<branch>-resend` branch is never detected and `git checkout -b <branch>-resend` fails with "already exists". The documented `-resend-2`/`-resend-3` fallback never triggers.
  WHY: A long session can hold a local `<branch>-resend` that was never pushed or was pushed to a name already taken on origin. A second fallback then passes the remote-only check and errors at `git checkout -b`, so the session must improvise. The fix is also to check `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>-resend` before `git checkout -b`.
- .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242 (same text in workflow-templates/.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:241-242; verified against .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1933-1938 and 2299-2300) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The doc says unconditionally that the guard (§21.B) allows this push because no PR has `<branch>-resend` as its head. That holds only when the GitHub API is reachable. In the §21.C fail-open path, `git_history_verdict` returns VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE and `_unreachable_outcome` calls `_request_confirmation`.
  WHY: A session following §21.F during a GitHub API outage expects the documented allow but gets a confirmation prompt. One clarifying sentence in the doc would close the gap.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
